Voynich MS - Quire 13

General

For an explanation of the material found on this page, see here.

Description

Quire 13 is composed of five bifolia instead of the standard four. It contains folios 75 through 84. The gathering mark is on f84v.

This quire contains all so-called biological pages. One page (f76r) contains only text. This is not the first page in the quire.

Tentative identifications

Four of the openings in the tube at the top of the page are ejecting something, and this has been considered to represent the four elements (left to right) air, water, fire, earth. To my best knowledge this was first noted by R. Santacoloma.

Other information

The two tubes of water coming out of the tub continue on the other folio that is part of this bifolio (f81r), which is invisible since another bifolio has been bound in between.

There is one character in line 26 that intrudes between two words of line 25 above. It is unclear if this is the result of specific planning. This character (  ) usually only appears in top lines of paragraphs.

General description

This is a so-called biological (or balneological) page. For general information about these pages see here.

Illustration(s)

There is a vertical structure of tubes in the left margin, populated by female figures. It ends in a green pool filling the entire width of the bottom of the page. In this pool, one female figure is standing in what looks like the mouth of a fish. There are four other animals near or in the water.

Text

This page has 42 text items (loci), as follows:
42 lines of standard text in paragraphs.

The text is in six paragraphs.

Currier language: B
RZ language: Bb+ (page) / Bb+ (folio) / Bb+ (bifolio)
LFD hand: 2

Browse interlinear transliteration of f79v

Tentative identifications

The woman / fish combination has been discussed a lot, and has been compared (among others) with a mermaid, with a female version of Jonah and the whale, and with the mythical creature Melusine.

One of the four animals in the bottom right has the same general posture as the lamb in the insignia of the golden fleece. This may well be completely coincidental.

Browse interlinear transliteration of f80v

Tentative identifications

The animal on the left has been compared with an armadillo, which is incompatible with the age of the MS.

A more realistic comparison can be made with a drawing of a ram as in one of the more famous copies of a German Hausbuch (>>see here). This is not at a definite identification, but just shows that there is no reason to believe that the drawing in the Voynich MS can only be an armadillo.

Other information

The tubes coming from the left margin are a continuation of tubes that have been drawn on f78v, which is not visible as another bifolio has been bound in between.

The reason for the unusual right margin is not known, but suggestions include that the text may be a poem, that the quality of the parchment did not allow writing, or that space was left for another drawing.

General description

This is a so-called biological (or balneological) page. For general information about these pages see here.
It has the folio nr (84) in the upper right corner.

Illustration(s)

There is a green pool with a roof accross the full width of the top of the page. It is populated by female figures that are standing mostly in pairs. Some of these may have crowns, or perhaps complicated hair-do's. A thin blue tube along the left margin leads to another pool in the middle, with green water and more nymphs. There is a separate small blue pool and one red bucket. A further thin blue tube leads to a round pool at the bottom, with faint blue water and many nymphs closely packed together.

Text

This page has 47 text items (loci), as follows:

11 nymph labels;
2 labels of 'tubs or tubes'.

The 34 lines of text are in five paragraphs. The last 10 lines are indented to the right of the bottom pool.

The tube labels are in the left margin. The text above the bottom pool is very wobbly, and could well be composed of individual labels, but it has been counted as (part of) a line of paragraph text.
